html:
The Pilatapa, or Pirlatapa, were an Aboriginal people of the northeast of South Australia, in the dry country between the Flinders Ranges and Cooper Creek. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

They are now counted as extinct as a separate people, and little of their language was written down. Neighbours on the map include the Wadigali, the Dieri and the Yandruwandha. Pastoral stations reached their country in the late 1800s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
